author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Prepare an EmuCoreX library handoff to a new Android phone
summary: Inventory game roots, firmware references, memory cards, profiles, controller layouts, and hashes as separate restore layers, rehearse the import into an isolated folder, and keep the old phone unchanged until the new one passes.
heroAlt: PCSX2 first-run wizard showing the separate firmware and game-directory choices that must be mapped on a new device

blocks.text: Separate portable data from device-specific choices

A phone migration contains at least four layers: personally dumped game and BIOS files, durable game progress, EmuCoreX profile exports and settings, and Android document permissions. Folder grants cannot simply be copied because the new phone issues its own URIs. Custom GPU drivers and renderer choices can also be wrong for a different SoC. Build a restore map rather than cloning an unexplained data directory.
Do not factory-reset, trade in, or erase the old phone until the new device has cold-booted representative games and reloaded native memory-card saves after its own reboot.
Create a migration manifest on the old device

items: Every active library root listed with storage type, relative files, bytes, and hashes.
A private BIOS dump inventory kept separate from game files.
Memory cards copied only after EmuCoreX is fully closed.
A dated per-game profile export and notes for custom controller layouts.
The old phone retained as a read-only recovery source during acceptance.

blocks.text: Restore by dependency, not by folder size

items: 1. Back up memory cards, save data, and profile JSON first; verify those small critical files before transferring large images.
2. Copy the verified BIOS and one known-good game to stable internal storage on the new phone.
3. Install the trusted EmuCoreX build, complete first run with Safe defaults, and grant the new device's own folder permissions.
4. Full-boot the test game, verify the native save, and confirm that Android retains access after restart.
5. Import the profile collection only after exporting the new phone's current empty or baseline collection; remember that import replaces the collection.
6. Review renderer and custom-driver fields against the new SoC before enabling them.
7. Add remaining library roots one at a time and reconcile counts plus hashes.
8. Test internal storage, removable storage, controller input, and one long session before declaring the handoff complete.

blocks.text: Android's automatic app backup may omit large files, app-specific exclusions, or user-selected document trees. Treat it as a convenience rather than proof. The manifest and independently verified user backups are the recovery authority.
Choose tests that cover every restored layer instead of launching the easiest title repeatedly.

items: New folder grants survive a device reboot.
A native memory-card save loads without a save state.
Profile count and selected exceptions match the dated export.
Renderer and GPU-driver choices suit the new hardware.
Representative CD, DVD, internal, and removable-storage games retain their hashes and cold-boot.

blocks.text: Migration symptoms and their owning layer

items: Library is empty but Files can browse it: reselect the document tree on the new phone.
Saves exist but game cannot see them: verify slot, region, and active data root.
Only profiled games crash: remove device-specific renderer or driver overrides.
Large images are missing: automatic Android backup did not include the external library.

blocks.text: Freeze the new device and return to the old reference

Stop adding data to the new phone, export its current profiles, and compare the restore map with the untouched old device. Replace only the failed layer: permission, image copy, card, or profile. Never copy the entire new data root back over the old one.

Once the new phone passes and independent backups are verified, remove private BIOS, saves, profiles, account sessions, and storage cards from the old device using the owner's planned secure-reset process. The Hub catalog does not need or accept copies of those private files.
